summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, tracheostomy, and multiple airway reconstructions was admitted due to persistent dysphagia, odynophagia, and cough over several weeks. She reported difficulty swallowing solids, pain at the trach site, and liquids going down the wrong way. A chest X-ray showed no pneumonia. A barium swallow study revealed upper pharyngeal edema, gastroesophageal reflux reaching the pharynx, and a small hiatal hernia, but no tracheoesophageal fistula. She was managed with optimized reflux treatment, dietary modifications, and speech therapy guidance. A periapical abscess was noted and referred for dental follow-up. She improved clinically and was discharged with instructions for continued reflux management, soft diet, and outpatient follow-up.
